cases.sentence: В народе среди мужчин и их жен поднялся сильный ропот на своих ___ иудеев.
cases.translation: A great cry rose among the men and their wives against their brothers the Jews.
cases.explain: The preposition на (against) here governs the accusative, but 'против своих братьев' uses genitive after 'сильный ропот на'; the verb requires genitive case for the object of the complaint.

cases.sentence: Нам нужно зерно, чтобы кормиться и жить, нам нужно ___.
cases.translation: We need grain to eat and live; we need grain.
cases.explain: The predicative nominative after the verb 'нужно' (need) takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Нам приходится закладывать свои поля, виноградники и дома, чтобы достать зерна во время ___.
cases.translation: We must pledge our fields, vineyards, and houses to get grain during the famine.
cases.explain: The preposition 'во время' (during) requires the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Я очень рассердился, услышав ропот и жалобы. Я обвинил ___ и начальствующих.
cases.translation: I was very angry when I heard their cry and complaints. I contended with the nobles and the rulers.
cases.explain: The transitive verb 'обвинил' (contended with/accused) takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Вы берете проценты со своих ___, — сказал я им.
cases.translation: You exact usury from your brothers, I said to them.
cases.explain: The preposition 'со' (with/from) requires the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Вернули бы им их поля, виноградники, масличные рощи и дома, а также проценты, которые вы им назначили, в руках их ___.
cases.translation: Return to them their fields, their vineyards, their olive orchards, and their houses, as well as the interest that you have charged them in their treasury.
cases.explain: The preposition 'в' (in) with location requires the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Еще я вытряхнул свою одежду и сказал, Так пусть же Бог вытряхнет всякого ___, который не сдержит этого обещания.
cases.translation: Then I shook out my lap and said, Thus may God shake out every man from his house who does not keep this promise.
cases.explain: The transitive verb 'вытряхнет' (shall shake out) governs the accusative case.

cases.sentence: С двадцатого ___ правления царя, я был назначен наместником в земле иудейской.
cases.translation: From the twentieth year of the reign of the king, I was appointed governor in the land of Judah.
cases.explain: The ordinal 'двадцатого' and temporal expressions with 'года' require the genitive case.

reading.ru: Прощение долгов беднякам В народе среди мужчин и их жен поднялся сильный ропот на своих братьев-иудеев.
reading.question: What rose among the people in the beginning of this chapter?
options: A great cry against their brothers the Jews
reading.correct: A great cry against their brothers the Jews
reading.explain: The text states 'поднялся сильный ропот на своих братьев-иудеев' — a great cry rose against their brothers the Jews.

reading.ru: Услышав их ропот и эти жалобы, я очень рассердился.
reading.question: How did Nehemiah react upon hearing the people's complaints?
reading.explain: The text says 'я очень рассердился' — I became very angry.

reading.ru: Вы берете проценты со своих братьев.
reading.question: What accusation did Nehemiah make against the nobles?
options: That they charged interest on their brothers
That they stole from the poor
That they refused to pay taxes
reading.correct: That they charged interest on their brothers
reading.explain: Nehemiah said 'Вы берете проценты со своих братьев' — You exact usury from your brothers.

reading.ru: Я, мои братья и слуги, также даем в долг народу деньги и зерно.
reading.question: What does Nehemiah say about his own lending practices?
options: He and his brothers also lend money and grain to the people
He only lends to the wealthy
reading.correct: He and his brothers also lend money and grain to the people
reading.explain: The text states 'Я, мои братья и слуги, также даем в долг народу деньги и зерно' — I, my brothers and servants, also lend money and grain to the people.

reading.ru: Прежние наместники, которые были до меня, возложили на народ тяжкое бремя и брали у них сорок шекелей серебра, помимо пищи и вина.
reading.question: How did the former governors treat the people?
options: They imposed a heavy burden and took forty shekels of silver plus food and wine
They gave money to the people
reading.correct: They imposed a heavy burden and took forty shekels of silver plus food and wine
reading.explain: The text says former governors 'возложили на народ тяжкое бремя и брали у них сорок шекелей серебра' — imposed a heavy burden and took forty shekels of silver from them.

reading.ru: Вспомни мне во благо, Боже мой, все, что я сделал для этого народа.
reading.question: What does Nehemiah ask God to remember at the end?
options: All the good things he has done for the people
The tribute owed to the king
reading.correct: All the good things he has done for the people
reading.explain: Nehemiah prays 'Вспомни мне во благо, Боже мой, все, что я сделал для этого народа' — Remember me for good, my God, all that I have done for this people.
